title: Natural spectral sequences and completion over a fixed admissible limit site
statement: Let (A,I) be a henselian pair with finitely generated I, and let U be the complement of V(I). Fix a small site (C,τ), an AdmissibleToposPresentation P for I on it, and the cartesian common-open embeddings j into the full-support blowups. There exists AdmissibleCompletionSpectralPresentation P j: completed-site projections on the same (C,τ), completed common-open embeddings, a cofinal extension and compatible blowup/closed-fibre/site comparisons, and original and completed AdmissibleSpectralPresentations, together with coefficient exchange normalized on every finite-stage coprojection, a natural spectral-sequence map with the prescribed E₂ square, preservation of torsion under the open completion pullback, and its canonical filtered cohomological abutment. All definitions and normalizations are those of [def-per-admissible-modification-presentation-data] and [def-per-admissible-modification-coefficient-data]. In particular this conclusion does not construct or assert existence of the original site, its limit property or its original common-open embeddings; those are fixed hypotheses.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.373: admissible blowups, (**) and its limit; p.374 final Note for the formal closed-fibre identification.

proof.text: Using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] with $R=\mathbf Z$, choose a nonnegative injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ and put $C_J=j_{J*}I^\bullet$ and $K_J=i_J^{-1}C_J$, where $i_J:Z_J\hookrightarrow B_J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives], $C_J$ represents $Rj_{J*}F$ and its derived global sections are represented by $\Gamma(B_J,C_J)=\Gamma(U,I^\bullet)$. For a domination $h:B_K\to B_J$ the ordinary exchange map $h^{-1}j_{J*}I^\bullet\to j_{K*}I^\bullet$ is adjoint to $j_{J*}I^\bullet\to h_*j_{K*}I^\bullet=j_{J*}I^\bullet$ equal to the identity. These maps satisfy composition and give the restricted coefficient system $K_J$. Exactness of inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] gives $H^q(K_J)=i_J^{-1}R^qj_{J*}F$. The open $U$ is quasi-compact because $I$ is finitely generated, so $j_J$ is qcqs. Apply [lem-sbc-qcqs-higher-images-prime-torsion] with all primes to see that these cohomology sheaves are torsion.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, finite-stage (**) and its limit; final Note.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-proper-henselian-derived-restriction] to the proper morphism $B_J\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the bounded-below torsion-cohomology complex $C_J$. It identifies the restriction map $R\Gamma(U,F)=R\Gamma(B_J,C_J)\to R\Gamma(Z_J,K_J)$ as an isomorphism. Its naturality clause applies to a domination and the exchange map of the preceding step. On $R\Gamma(U,F)$ that map is the identity: its adjoint defining $j_{J*}I^\bullet\to h_*j_{K*}I^\bullet$ is the identity, so the global-section map is the identity on $\Gamma(U,I^\bullet)$. Thus the whole diagram of derived sections is canonically identified with the constant diagram $R\Gamma(U,F)$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, finite-stage (**) and its limit; final Note.

proof.text: Set $K=\varinjlim_Jp_J^{-1}K_J$ termwise. Apply [lem-per-finite-cover-derived-sections-continuity] with common lower bound zero. It gives $R\Gamma(\mathcal T,K)\simeq\operatorname{colim}^{\mathrm{der}}_JR\Gamma(Z_J,K_J)\simeq R\Gamma(U,F)$; the last identification uses the constant diagram of Step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram]. Inverse image on abelian sheaves is exact [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact], and filtered colimits of abelian sheaves are exact [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact]. They therefore preserve the kernels and cokernels defining cohomology, giving $H^q(K)=\varinjlim_Jp_J^{-1}i_J^{-1}R^qj_{J*}F=L_F^q$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, finite-stage (**) and its limit; final Note.

proof.text: The category of abelian sheaves on the presenting small site is Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] with the constant ring $\mathbf Z$. Apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to its global-section functor and $K$, with lower bound zero. Its $E_2$ formula is $H^p(\mathcal T,H^qK)=H^p(\mathcal T,L_F^q)$, and Step 5 identifies its abutment with $H^{p+q}(U,F)$. Its stated finite filtration is $\mathrm{Fil}^pH^n=\operatorname{im}(H^n(R\Gamma\tau_{\le n-p}K)\to H^n(R\Gamma K))$, giving exactly $n+1$ graded pieces and no unbounded convergence issue.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, finite-stage (**) and its limit; final Note.

proof.text: Since $I$ is finitely generated, [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] makes $A'$ complete for $IA'$ and identifies $A'/IA'$ with $A/I$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian] makes $(A',IA')$ henselian; proper-pair restriction applies on the completed side too. By [lem-per-admissible-modification-system], extension of ideals is cofinal and the corresponding closed fibres are compatibly isomorphic. The reindexing clause of [lem-per-qcqs-etale-topos-inverse-limit] therefore gives the common $\mathcal T$. The completion pullback/exchange maps, computed on resolutions by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise], of the open direct images restrict and then pass to colimits to give $K\to K'$ in $D^+(\mathcal T)$; their cohomology maps are exactly $L_F^q\to L_{F'}^q$. Naturality of proper-pair restriction [lem-per-proper-henselian-derived-restriction] and of derived site continuity [lem-per-finite-cover-derived-sections-continuity] identifies the induced $R\Gamma$ arrow with the canonical $R\Gamma(U,F)\to R\Gamma(U',F')$. Apply [lem-pc-raw-truncation-couple-naturality] to $K\to K'$: it gives maps of the truncation couples of Step 6 commuting with $\alpha,f,g$, with the abutment maps $c_n$ and with the $E_2$ identifications. Then [lem-sp-derived-couple-functoriality] gives the induced maps on every page, the required spectral-sequence morphism. They preserve the abutment filtration because the truncation inclusions are natural, and each filtration step in Step 6 is the image of that inclusion. This also proves naturality in $F$. Nothing here asserts that $K\to K'$ or its cohomology sheaves are isomorphisms. The original site and open embeddings are fixed inputs. Use the two-dimensional limit property to transport the finite-cover construction onto that site, and choose the completed site projection functors and siteComparison using the canonical cofinal comparison. They are constructed together, rather than quantified as arbitrary incompatible projections. This gives the remaining data AdmissibleCompletionSpectralPresentation over those fixed original inputs.

lean.statement: theorem admissibleCompletionSpectralPresentation {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [HenselianRing A I] (hI : I.FG) (U : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Opens) (hU : ∀ x : PrimeSpectrum A, x ∈ U ↔ x ∉ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A)) {C : Type (u + 1)} [SmallCategory C] {τ : GrothendieckTopology C} (P : AdmissibleToposPresentation I C τ) (j : AdmissibleOpenEmbeddings I U) : Nonempty (AdmissibleCompletionSpectralPresentation P j)
lean.note: The original topos and open embeddings are parameters; the auxiliary structure contains exactly the remaining completion and spectral-sequence data.
